Foundation Space Resources (FSR) is a for-profit company specializing in advanced modelling and simulation technologies for the space industry. Established on October 14, 2020, in Alberta, Canada, FSR has rapidly positioned itself as a leader in Lunar mission planning, environmental simulation, and system modelling, catering to space agencies, research institutions, and private aerospace firms.
With a lean but highly specialized team, FSR has successfully developed innovative Digital Twin technology to address critical gaps in Lunar exploration. The company has actively engaged in industry partnerships and secured interest from key stakeholders and customers such as Canadensys, Starpath Robotics (Starpath), Space Copy, Orbit Share, and the North American Space Institute (NASI).

FSR's Lunar Digital Twin is the only commercially available tool which can provide high temporal and spatial fidelity illumination maps of the entire Lunar surface, including the 3-dimensional structure of shadows above the surface. Customers are currently using it to quantify (and thereby optimize) hardware design constraints and develop flexible mission plans. Currently TRL 4, it simulates the components of and the interactions between the different aspects of the cislunar (i.e. between the Earth and the Moon) environment. FSR's near-term goal is to develop our Lunar Digital Twin into a flexible tool for Lunar hardware design constraint and mission planning optimization. Our long-term vision is to develop our Digital Twin into a comprehensive dynamic simulation of the Lunar environment, capable of supporting automated virtual testing, economic assessments, demand analysis for Lunar services, and mission planning as well as be deployed on Lunar assets to aid in navigation. FSR is enhancing this tool with recent advances in AI, including explainability and evolutionary algorithms to optimize hardware design, mission planning, and decision-making processes.

FSR aims to meet the growing demand for high-fidelity Lunar modelling and simulation capabilities arising from the developing awareness of the commercial Lunar industry that current design and testing methodologies do not sufficiently de-risk hardware designs and mission plans to meet desired mission timelines and profitability. High-fidelity Lunar modelling and simulation capabilities are not only critical for mission planning and system design but are also vital for the verification, validation, and stress testing of space systems.

Promote the attainment and maintenance of excellence in the standard and quality of research and innovation.

Support the undertaking of research and innovation in all fields of activity and disciplines by researchers with different levels of knowledge, experience and specialist skills in such fields or disciplines.

Promote and support the contribution made by research and innovation to economic, social, cultural and environmental development and sustainability in the State.

Strengthen the engagement of the research and innovation system with:

>the Government, Ministers of the Government and bodies (whether statutory or otherwise) which are funded wholly or partly by public moneys, and

ABOUT US
Founded in 1997, Tesera Systems Inc. (Tesera) is an employee–owned technology company. Tesera is 100% exclusively focused on delivering High Resolution Inventory Solutions (HRIS).

In business for over 26 years, our interdisciplinary team reflects a unique combination of forestry and data IT skills and experience. We pride ourselves on providing clients with responsive, exceptional services, high-quality, fully managed and transparent forest and natural resource inventory solutions.

Across Canada, the USA, Brazil and South Africa (in both natural and plantation forests), our team have now successfully completed 17 HRIS Enhanced Forest Inventories (EFI) projects on different forested landscapes covering almost 650,000 hectares, and Individual Tree Inventories (ITI) on a subset of 141,632 hectares.

OUR SOLUTIONS

HRIS integrates AI-based, machine learning and advanced analytics with Enhanced Forest Inventory (EFI) and Individual Tree Inventory (ITI) capabilities.

Tesera has designed HRIS to use fixed radius ground plots and a range of remote sensing data, including LiDAR, 4-band color infrared imagery, and multispectral satellite imagery. HRIS can accommodate terrain and soils, climate and other ancillary data.

HRIS uses advanced data science, AI-based machine learning (ML) and automation using Amazon Web Services to process forest inventory data. HRIS generates over 1,300 features for use in developing models to predict accurate and reliable forest attributes including tree species, heights, diameters, volumes, forest stand structure, site productivity and many others.

Our unique and transparent approach to data aggregation and analytics empowers our clients to discover hidden and sustainable opportunities, and realize new value from their forestry and natural resource assets. HRIS solutions are accurate, flexible and fully scalable… from small woodlands to extensive forest and natural resource landscapes covering millions of acres and hectares.

Over multiple projects and diverse forest conditions, HRIS is more accurate, with an increase in predictive accuracy of 66% (or three times more accurate). This means that in order to achieve the same accuracy with a conventional ground plot-based approach, one would need to establish at least 9 times the number of ground plots.

Our AI-based machine learning inventory solutions are extremely versatile and continue to support multiple data sources and applications. For example, HRIS is serving as the basis for determining forest carbon stocks, carbon offsets (sequestration and abatement) and will be used to model forest changes over time. HRIS is also providing an accurate and reliable approach to support several carbon and forest harvesting projects, ensuring independent data verification and adherence to established standards and regulations. Additional insights on some of these projects can be found at: www.tesera.com/projects.

Our team is also advancing the automation of multivariate forest change detection using advanced algorithms and analytics to rapidly and accurately identify changes in forest environments. This approach requires analyzing multiple variables and large datasets (time series satellite imagery, climate data and other environmental indicators) to detect and monitor changes in forest cover, health and composition over time.

entityName: The European Marine Energy Centre Limited
entityDescription:
EMEC is a not-for-profit innovation catalyst pioneering the transition to a clean energy future.
Established in 2003, EMEC is the world’s leading centre for demonstrating wave and tidal energy converters in the sea.
As a plug-and-play facility EMEC helps reduce the time, cost and risk of testing innovative sustainable technologies.
EMEC is the world’s only accredited ocean energy test laboratory (ISO/IEC 17025) and inspection body (ISO/IEC 17020): the centre provides pre-consented grid-connected test sites in harsh wave and tidal regimes as well as scale test sites in gentler conditions for testing smaller scale technologies, subsystems and components. To date, EMEC has hosted more ocean energy devices than at any other site, providing operational, technical and business support to help clients commercialise.
Attracting developers from around the globe, EMEC’s facilities help to prove what is achievable in some of the harshest marine environments while in close proximity to sheltered waters and harbours.
Building on our experience in developing the ocean energy sector, EMEC is exploring options for developing a national floating offshore wind test site to the west of Orkney. The site aims to offer floating wind developers representative metocean conditions to those in ScotWind, Celtic Seas and future leasing rounds. EMEC also runs the Offshore Wind R&I Programme searching for novel solutions to help deliver offshore wind faster, cheaper and at lower risk.
EMEC is also leading innovation projects exploring the integration of renewables with green hydrogen, storage and e-fuels. The centre has established an R&D hydrogen ecosystem, featuring electrolysers, fuel cells, storage and refuelling, for first-of-a-kind and pilot scale projects aiming to decarbonise power, heat and transport applications.
EMEC’s infrastructure and experience are increasingly being used in wider energy systems and decarbonisation innovation. For example, Microsoft demonstrated a subsea data centre at EMEC’s offshore test site and EMEC is leading the Islands Centre for Net Zero to support Orkney, Shetland and the Outer Hebrides on their path to net zero emissions.
EMEC was set up in 2003 to kick start an ocean energy sector in the UK and boost economic development in the Highlands and Islands. Over the years EMEC has grown and diversified, and unprecedented activity that has taken place in Orkney due to the presence of EMEC has been a catalyst for economic development, creating jobs and a world-leading supply chain now exporting skills and knowledge around the globe. An economic impact assessment calculated EMEC added £370 million GVA to the UK economy between 2003 and 2023.

Furthermore, astronauts are trained, space experiments are prepared and sounding rockets are developed and launched from sites around the world. Eventually, DLR works on new technologies, such as on-orbit-servicing in order to master even the most difficult space projects of the future.
